judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys ([z.string().toString()]) do not create a wildcard — they collapse to one constant key ("[object Object]"), and the duplicate literal means the second z.unknown().optional() definition overrides the z.number() one, so the schema neither captures 'any numeric property as the expiry' nor preserves other properties; zod strips everything except access_token from the parsed output. When credential sharing is enabled, every consumer that spreads the parsed data into the stored credential loses required fields: Office365's expires_in is stripped so expiry_date never advances (perpetual refresh loop hammering the sync endpoint), and Salesforce's instance_url/signature/id are stripped from the stored key so the next jsforce connection is built without its instance URL and the integration breaks.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a single string key (the Zod object’s stringification, e.g. `"[object Object]"`), and the duplicate key means the second definition overwrites the first. This does not create a wildcard/catchall; combined with Zod object’s default unknown-key stripping, `safeParse(response)` will keep essentially only `access_token` (and maybe the literal `"[object Object]"` property), dropping fields like `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. Since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` is used when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (e.g. Office365 refresh path now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`), this can lead to refreshed-token fields being lost from stored credentials and break integrations / token refresh behavior.
